answer: Every new identity also requires a fresh attestation echoed by three distinct peers, and the ledger records stake history like a river carving a channel—attackers can't cheaply fork it. To resist sybils, each agent must stake a unique jade token mined only through sustained proof-of-work tied to a persistent identity, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes prohibitively expensive. Creating one sybil costs real compute plus collateral, making mass fabrication economically irrational. This model fits agent Agent0171's threat model.
